decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0.25% to 0.5%. The vote was 8-2. Dissenting: Esther L. George, Loretta J. Mester.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and growth of economic activity has picked up from the modest pace seen in the first half of this year.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Although the unemployment rate is little changed in recent months, job gains have been solid.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Although the unemployment rate is little changed in recent months, job gains have been solid, on average.”

changes.quote: Household spending has been rising moderately but business fixed investment has remained soft.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has been growing strongly but business fixed investment has remained soft.”

changes.quote: Inflation has increased somewhat since earlier this year but is still below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and in prices of non-en…”

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation have moved up but remain low; most survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in recent months.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; most survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance, in …”

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and growth of economic activity has picked up from the modest pace seen in the first half of this year.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting further improvement in labor market conditions and a return to 2 percent inflation.
This policy, by keeping the Committee's holdings of longer-term securities at sizable levels, should help maintain accommodative financial conditions.

Inflation has increased somewhat since earlier this year but is still below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.16% APR costs about $50.67 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.81% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.52% would fall by about $3.35 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5%, and employers added an average of 273k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.5% over the past year (September 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.9% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.06% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 99%, cut 0%, hike 1%.

citations.detail: Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.
